Last updated November 14, 2026.

Utah property tax is assessed and collected at the local level, and owners can appeal an assessment.

What the official sources say

  • A taxpayer dissatisfied with the valuation or equalization of real property may apply to appeal to the county board of equalization. (Utah Code 59-2-1004(2); source)
  • The application is due on or before the later of September 15 of the current year or the last day of a 45-day period beginning on the day the county auditor provides the valuation notice (59-2-919.1). (Utah Code 59-2-1004(3)(a); source)
  • The county board of equalization must decide each appeal within 60 days after the application is made (the Tax Commission may approve an extension). (Utah Code 59-2-1004(8)(c)-(d); source)
  • A taxpayer dissatisfied with the county board's decision may appeal to the State Tax Commission under 59-2-1006. (Utah Code 59-2-1004(10); source)
  • Tangible taxable property is assessed and taxed at a uniform and equal rate on the basis of fair market value as valued on January 1 (no separate assessment ratio is stated in this subsection). (Utah Code 59-2-103(2); source)
  • Property may be redeemed by any person before the tax sale, which is held after four years from the date the taxes became delinquent. (Utah Code 59-2-1346(1); source)
  • Redemption requires paying the county treasurer all delinquent taxes, tax notice charges, interest, penalties and administrative costs. (Utah Code 59-2-1346(2); source)

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Utah offers property tax relief for qualifying homeowners, and official sources explain the rules.

What the official sources say

  • Residential property is allowed a residential exemption equal to a 45% reduction in fair market value for a calendar year (subject to other provisions). (Utah Code 59-2-103(3); source)
  • The residential exemption is limited to one primary residence per household (with exceptions in 59-2-103(6)(b)). (Utah Code 59-2-103(6)(a); source)
  • Utah Exemptions Act homestead (creditor protection): up to $42,000 in value if the property is the individual's primary personal residence; $5,000 otherwise. (Utah Code 78B-5-503(2)(a); source)
  • For jointly owned primary residences each owner is entitled to an exemption, with a maximum of $84,000 per household. (Utah Code 78B-5-503(2)(b); source)

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Utah evictions follow notice and court steps set by state law.

What the official sources say

  • Nonpayment: tenant is in unlawful detainer after a written notice to pay or surrender has gone uncomplied with for three business days after service. (Utah Code 78B-6-802; source)
  • Tenancy at will: unlawful detainer if tenant remains after a notice of not less than five calendar days. (Utah Code 78B-6-802; source)
  • Landlord gives written notice, files complaint and summons, serves tenant; tenant has 3 business days to answer or default can be sought. (Utah Courts self-help: Eviction Information for Landlords; source)
  • Order of Eviction requires the tenant to leave within 3 calendar days of receiving it; only a sheriff or constable can enforce it. (Utah Courts self-help: Eviction Information for Landlords; source)
  • If the tenant answers, an occupancy hearing is scheduled within 10 days of request; trial within 60 days if more information is needed. (Utah Courts self-help: Eviction Information for Landlords; source)
  • After a foreclosure sale, tenants may be allowed under federal law to stay until the lease expires or 90 days after sale, whichever is later. (Utah Code 78B-6-901.5; source)

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Utah counties hold tax sales of delinquent property.

What the official sources say

  • Property may be redeemed by any person before the tax sale, which is held after four years from the date the taxes became delinquent. (Utah Code 59-2-1346(1); source)
  • Redemption requires paying the county treasurer all delinquent taxes, tax notice charges, interest, penalties and administrative costs. (Utah Code 59-2-1346(2); source)
  • The county auditor conducts the tax sale in May or June, at the courthouse front door or electronically. (Utah Code 59-2-1351(1); source)
  • Notice of tax sale is mailed to the last known recorded owner, the occupant of improved property, and other interests of record as of the preceding March 15. (Utah Code 59-2-1351(2); source)
  • Sale is public auction to the highest bidder for cash; a bid below total taxes, charges, interest, penalty and costs is not accepted. (Utah Code 59-2-1351(4); source)
  • A tax upon real property is a lien against the property assessed. (Utah Code 59-2-1325(1)(a); source)
  • The property tax lien attaches on January 1 of each year. (Utah Code 59-2-1325(1)(c); source)
